items.name: jixoai-theme
items.title: jixoai theme
items.description: The jixoai design-language token sheet: OKLCH colors with the one-brand-hue law, hard offset shadows, radius 0 with bevel upgrade, mono-first fonts, terminal surfaces, and the data-reveal entrance styles (static markup + CSS).
items.docs: Install delivers the full token sheet as a css FILE (jixoai.css). No cssVars are injected: injection overwrote existing brand hues and produced mangled mappings on projects that already carried a token sheet.

items.name: toc-engine
items.title: ToC geometry engine
items.description: Framework-free table-of-contents engine: per-frame geometry snapshot computes IoM weights (intersection area / min(block, viewport) — saturates to 100% in both directions) and the line pick (the viewport-top line resolves to the region containing it; margins resolve DOWNWARD to the next block; mobile line sits at the sticky bar bottom + 2em). Region source is [data-region]/[data-family] markup, OR — new in the scroll-area family (2026-08-22) — a derived-extents provider (the toc-outline lib): heading extents synthesized at compute time, re-read live every pass.
items.docs: Observe regions with data-region on leaf heading-to-heading blocks and data-family on parent section extents. The engine calls onUpdate(weights: Map<id, 0..1>, pick: id | null) on scroll/resize (rAF-throttled).

items.name: press-button
items.title: Press button
items.description: The press-law button (theme .jx-press): hover grows the shadow only (xs → sm, the body never moves); active presses the body +1px into the page while the box-shadow offsets counter-shrink 1px (the *-press token poses) — the shadow paint stays anchored, no pseudo layer. Variant ladder: fill / tonal / outline (default) / ghost + link (an interaction-affordance exception, not a surface rung); hue is injection through --jx-fill/--jx-fill-ink/--jx-tonal/--jx-outline (destructive ACTIONS inject the destructive pair, copied-style feedback = tonal + success). One opt-in effect loop per button via typed builders exported from the module script — shimmer() additive perimeter spark (plus-lighter, box-owned clip), pulse() sonar rings (slow/ring/ripple), rainbow() blended aurora wash (conic, three prime timelines, screen on fill / color elsewhere), ripple() press-point ink driven by WAAPI and removed on animation.finished (runtime extracted to ripple.svelte.ts, shared with Chip), with a round/bevel-diamond shape option — modeled on the animation-svelte reference, options on every loop, frozen under reduced motion.

items.name: list-item
items.title: List item
items.description: The list row as a system (F7 coverage, shadcn composition): AUTO-VARIANT chrome — standalone rows carry their own terminal surface, ItemGroup owns the frame (native section+ul, default/muted/plain modes, optional label, divider policy: 38% auto hairlines structurally exclusive with full-strength ItemDivider). The ItemEnd lane hosts after/actions/chevron; the grid presence matrix stays four bits (:has()-driven, no implicit tracks). ItemField wires settings rows (label[for], describedby chains) and five thin adapters — ItemToggle/ItemCheckbox/ItemRadio/ItemSelect/ItemInput — compose the existing controls without reimplementing them. layout=media rides custom properties; narrow groups wrap the end lane at 30rem via container query.

items.name: section-card
items.title: Section card
items.description: The content atom of the jixoai site grammar: bordered card, header block with eyebrow (brand hue, Share Tech Mono, tracked), font-nav title, text-pretty summary, body snippet slot.

items.name: figure
items.title: Figure
items.description: The ontology's 浮 line primitive: a native <figure> that numbers itself from its Section's numbering domain — chapter-scoped per kind (Eq 4.5) or document-continuous by floatScope declaration. The wrapper owns structure (number/anchor/caption, the display currency of DOM order — reorder renumbers); any point nests inside as the content slot (composition-first: the line carries structure, the point carries industry semantics). citedIn is the manual backlink lane (display-currency strings rendered verbatim + emitted as JSON) while automatic backlink rendering stays a documented harvest-only gap. The family folder also ships the frozen R2 interface module (numbering.svelte.ts: TargetRegistry, NumberingDomain/DomainRegistry, the pure ordinal derivation) and the route-page NumberingProvider that owns the document-level observer lifecycle.

items.name: reference
items.title: Reference
items.description: The ontology's 引 primitive: a typed cross-link with zero grammar knowledge of its own — resolution follows the target through the route-page document registry (an equation Figure renders Eq (4.5), a numbered Section § 3.2.1, an unnumbered one its title). The resolved state is a native fragment anchor (keyboard/ARIA ride the platform); a missing target degrades loudly to a visible ??(id) marker that never throws. Edge emission splits by state: not-yet-registered (the whole SSR pass) keeps the data-ref-to claim for the static harvester's two-pass pre-scan, while a settled miss drops the edge (dead anchors are a filed bug class). The children snippet replaces the anchor's label text only.

items.name: terminal-header
items.title: Terminal header
items.description: The site header as composed chrome: the bar shell, brand block, pill box with its sliding indicator, and the mobile drawer — the NAVIGATION is composed NavigationMenuItem/Trigger/Panel parts (consumer-authored mega grids) with bare NavigationMenuLinks; the three-level TerminalNavItem config tree is dead. closeAll() hides every open popover under the header; open is bindable for the drawer.

items.name: terminal-footer
items.title: Terminal footer
items.description: The site footer as composed chrome: TerminalFooter owns the © row + ghost fallback; TerminalFooterColumn (title + free link children) composes the columns.

items.name: theme-toggle
items.title: Theme toggle
items.description: light / dark / system control in four variants: full (segmented icon+label selector), compact (icon + current), icon (icon only), text (label only). Inline SVG icons, no icon-library dependency; shared theme contract (localStorage theme, .dark + colorScheme).
items.docs: Props: variant 'full'|'compact'|'icon'|'text', hideLabels? (full only), labels? { light, dark, system, groupAriaLabel? } — localize the mode vocabulary and the group aria name; absent = the shipped English, and the localStorage 'theme' value domain is never localized.

items.name: toc
items.title: Combo ToC
items.description: The reading rail as a composed family: manual mode composes TocList/TocItem/TocLink(child) — a legal list tree (anchors never nest); AUTO mode (outline: TocOutlineConfig) derives from headings at runtime — the DECLARED SSR exception (rail shell first, links on hydrate). Scrollspy is Root behavior, DOM-delegated.
items.docs: Give the outline as sections/children props; the component renders desktop + mobile surfaces and wires the engine. Content needs non-overlapping data-region wrappers and data-family section extents (see toc-engine docs). AUTO mode derives the outline through the toc-outline lib (a declared registry dependency — installed with the item). topLayer?: boolean (default auto) — when a website-scaffold top layer exists via the jx-top-layer context, the rail self-adopts into it; pass topLayer={false} to keep classic in-flow behavior.

items.name: website-scaffold
items.title: Website scaffold
items.description: WebsiteScaffold — the page scaffold for presentation sites (traditional websites) around terminal-header: a sticky, always-visible header band (navigation never scrolls away), main column, optional footer, and a skip link. Ships the systematized MPA view transitions: cross-document navigation with a persistent site-header and a horizontal-slide + blur crossfade on page-main (reduced-motion degrades to crossfade). Pair with view-transitions-toolkit's useAutoTypes() (render-blocking) for from-/to-route typed variants. Renamed from app-shell: an AppScaffold for application-style sites is a separate future design.
items.docs: Slots: header (required), children (main), footer (optional). Import website-scaffold.css once. Publishes the jx-top-layer context (ordered multi-node adopt/release into .jx-float-slot) — scaffold-float portals through it and the toc rail self-mounts automatically. For route-typed transitions, wire useAutoTypes({ index: '/', components: '/components', ... }) in a render-blocking module in <head> (view-transitions-toolkit/navigation).

items.name: ghostty-term
items.title: Ghostty term
items.description: The brand's live terminal surface: a DPR-aware canvas grid rendered by the real libghostty-vt wasm with rAF-batched dirty-row painting, density-derived cell metrics (--jx-text/--jx-line), auto (ResizeObserver) or explicit cols/rows sizing, and the onData input bridge (keyEncode, paste-gated, wheel scroll). Shell paper/ink resolve from jixoai terminal tokens; ANSI/256/truecolor content colors pass through verbatim. wasm url comes from the virtual:jixoai-ghostty plugin module or the wasmUrl prop; load failure degrades to data-state=error with a terminal-styled fallback (children slot owns the face).
items.docs: Props: cols, rows, auto (default true; explicit cols/rows fixes the grid), fontSize (px, finite positive), wasmUrl, theme {background,foreground}, onData(bytes), onResize({cols,rows}), density, class, children (overlay + error-face owner), ...rest. bind:this: write(bytes) / reset() / resizeTo(cols,rows) / snapshot(). Install prerequisite: the jixoai vite plugin (virtual:jixoai-ghostty).

items.name: terminal-card
items.title: Terminal card
items.description: The Broadside hero terminal, composed after the openspecui reference: traffic-light title bar, one large typed command line, outputs surfacing line by line, 6px hard offset shadow. One-shot typing entrance (never looping), static block cursor (jixoai motion law), prerendered/no-JS shows the settled terminal, reduced motion renders instantly.
items.docs: Props: barTitle, command, outputs: readonly string[].

items.name: hero-section
items.title: Hero section
items.description: The landing hero with opened content: title/badges/terminal/secondary/copy are snippets (the caller composes Badge children; the default copy CTA rides the copyCommand payload; the em accent paint lives in family css).
items.docs: Props: eyebrow, titleLead, titleAccent, summary, badges: readonly string[], copyCommand (snippet-conditional: required when the DEFAULT copy CTA renders; optional when a #copy snippet replaces it), copyLabel?, terminal snippet, secondary? snippet.

items.name: language-switcher
items.title: Language switcher
items.description: Locale switching in two variants: pair (icon + segmented two-locale group, active fills brand hue — composed after the openspecui bilingual reference) and menu (icon + current-locale button with a hard-shadow dropdown for three or more locales). Anchor-based (each locale carries its href) so it works on fully prerendered sites; terminal-surface styling matches theme-toggle.
items.docs: Props: variant 'pair'|'menu', locales: { code, label, href }[], current (code), ariaLabel?. The menu closes on select, outside click, and Escape. Clicking a locale persists its code to localStorage key 'lang' (the site's language-negotiation bootstrap reads the same key); navigation stays pure anchors, so prerendered sites keep working.

items.name: card-grid
items.title: Card grid
items.description: Grid + subgrid layout that equalizes cards: shared header row and body row, so headers align and bodies fill to the tallest — no ragged tops or unequal bottoms. Columns are auto-fit minmax (responsive; min prop controls collapse width, default 320px). The foot prop declares a third shared row so zone-trio cards (head/body/foot, e.g. the card component) also align their feet at band bottoms. Works with any card whose first child is the header block (section-card unchanged); no-subgrid browsers fall back to stacked rows.
items.docs: Props: min (CSS length, default '320px'), foot (boolean, declares the third shared row for head/body/foot cards). Wrap cards as direct children; opt a child out with data-no-subgrid.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: The structural surface — the dialog row ruler's static clone: head/body/foot zones with stamped presence, edge-riding structural separators, the body-only scroll law, and an open inline-end actions slot (no close button ships). Zones place by integer cell lines, so the card qualifies as a card-grid child unchanged. Designed as the foundation dialog will sit on.
items.docs: Props: title?, head? (flush head override), actions? (the inline-end slot — dialog's × seat), foot? (raw foot override; the standard face is CardFooter), scroll = true (body scroll authority; false retires it with the gutter), class?, children. CardHeader: title? / children. CardFooter: start? (inline-start seat), end? (raw inline-end), label, children (auto one ButtonGroup, leadingSeam).

items.name: jx-pure
items.title: jx-pure — the componentless face (Tier 0)
items.description: One stylesheet, the whole jixoai face, zero JS: mount class jx-pure on any DOM and the subtree's BARE native elements get the law — Pico-style element defaults in @layer components (:where-scoped, so utilities always win) for typography, links, buttons (press physics), text-like inputs (TYPE ALLOWLIST), checkbox/radio repaints, the zero-JS range fill (cqw shadow technique, daisyUI-inspired), color repaints, fieldset/legend, details/summary, nav/ol/ul/dl, tables — PLUS the migrated native-form class vocabulary verbatim (.jx-field/.jx-label/.jx-error/.jx-control/.jx-control-shell/.jx-control-lane/.jx-slider/.jx-color-shell/.jx-color-swatch/.jx-color-expand, the Tier-2 frozen contract — the Part A region is also sliced byte-exact into the generated @jixoai/jx-native-contract item for component installs). Dark mode rides the token sheet's .dark/.jx-light (color-scheme inherits from the scope root). select keeps its platform arrow by default; .jx-select opts into the gradient chevron repaint (single-select only). progress/meter ride the 8px track family with token-mapped semantic fills (primary/secondary/destructive), output is the mono result lane, figure/figcaption carry the caption law; no-jx-pure (per-rule :not() exclusion) reverts a whole subtree to UA paint (the escape hatch); Part D (generated from the token sheet by scripts/gen-jx-auto-dark.mjs) gives zero-JS static pages OS-following dark via the .jx-auto-dark class. Floating surfaces (dialog/popover/tooltip) stay Tier-2 by boundary.
items.docs: Import once from the site css, AFTER the token sheet: @import './lib/jixoai.css'; @import './lib/jx-pure.css'; — then mount the class: <main class="jx-pure">…bare HTML…</main>. Static no-JS pages: theme with <html class="dark"> (or any ancestor); OS-follow dark is ALSO zero JS via the generated .jx-auto-dark class — <html class="jx-pure jx-auto-dark"> (never inside .jx-light; an explicit .dark always wins; a host bootstrap remains the explicit-toggle JS alternative). The Part A region ships byte-exact as @jixoai/jx-native-contract (component installs depend on the extract, not this full face). Glyph data-URIs mirror icons.ts (calendar/clock/pipette) — edit both or neither. Reverse scope: mount no-jx-pure — the face steps aside (per-rule :not()), host styles survive.

items.name: native-form
items.title: Native form layer (Tier 1) — DEPRECATED alias of jx-pure
items.description: DEPRECATED (2026-08-23): the native form layer was absorbed into jx-pure (same source file, same class vocabulary, verbatim). This alias keeps the old install name and target path working for one release window — new code should install @jixoai/jx-pure. The Tier-2 components (input/range/number-input) now declare @jixoai/jx-pure as their dependency.
items.docs: Alias of @jixoai/jx-pure — install that instead: same css (Part A is the native-form sheet verbatim), plus the .jx-pure element face. Import path stays @lib/native-form.css for existing installs until the alias retires.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: NativeHTML input: every native type passes through. Text-like types get the jixoai shell (1px border, radius 0, hover lift, inset focus ring) with the Tier-1 lane (.jx-input-lane) inside; range is the Tier-1 pure-CSS slider (.jx-range); color is the Tier-1 color field (.jx-color-field wrapper, locked square swatch, pipette glyph); date/time/number lanes restyle the platform's picker indicator and spinners via the same sheet. checkbox/radio/toggle/file have their own components (the bare types still pass through). Optional label[for], error wiring (aria-invalid + aria-describedby, monochrome dashed ! message), clearable ×, four snippet slots. value is $bindable: bound = controlled, absent = purely uncontrolled (FormData/form.reset untouched).
items.docs: Props: type, label?, error?, clearable?, innerInlineStart/innerInlineEnd/outerBlockStart/outerBlockEnd snippets, id? (auto), class, value ($bindable), ...restProps passed to the native input.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: Custom select built on the native Popover API + CSS Anchor Positioning: popover='auto' light-dismiss panel, listbox role with roving aria-activedescendant (↑↓/Home/End/Enter), terminal bezel styling with primary left-border selected state, RTL-aware. name= submits the committed VALUE into FormData through the faceless form-field bridge (ElementInternals); for the platform's own overlay picker use native-select instead. Floating-surface law: ::after shadow layer (semi-transparent black/white) + @starting-style entry; variant='solid' | 'acrylic' | 'auto' (acrylic falls back to solid under prefers-reduced-transparency; the terminal bezel keeps its identity through the jx-surface fill props).

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: NativeHTML textarea with the jixoai text shell; rows pass-through (default 4), resize: vertical. Same label/error contract as input.

items.name: scaffold-float
items.title: Scaffold float portal
items.description: The consumer-side half of the WebsiteScaffold float provider: renders children into the scaffold's top layer (.jx-top-layer) through a real portal — nodes are created here (full Svelte ownership) and adopted into the provider's insertion point on mount. The float rides the top layer's immersive hide/reveal with the header by construction.
items.docs: Slot children; pairs with website-scaffold's jx-top-layer context (ordered multi-node adopt/release — the same mechanism the toc uses to self-mount).

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: NativeHTML dialog: native <dialog> + showModal() (focus trap, Escape, top layer). Floating-surface law: ::after shadow layer + @starting-style pull-apart entry; variant='solid' | 'acrylic' | 'auto'; scrim = --scrim (semi-transparent black/white, never a brand tint); the 460ms WAAPI --jx-p timeline presses the layers back together.
items.docs: Props: title?, open ($bindable), variant?, class? (geometry-only), scroll? (default true — the body zone's scroll authority; false retires it with the stable both-edges gutter reservation), cancelGuard?; snippets children, head? (custom flush head, typically <DialogHeader>), footer? (the RAW full foot override — usually a <DialogFooter>: children auto-join one end-packed ButtonGroup with ghost seams and the leadingSeam bracket, ghost via the zone's Context scope; the end slot replaces the grouped arrangement). Escape goes through the cancel event and shares the animated close path.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: NativeHTML popover: the native Popover API base (popover='auto' light dismiss, popovertarget trigger, CSS Anchor Positioning). Floating-surface law: the hard offset shadow is a REAL ::after layer pulled apart by an @starting-style entry; variant='solid' | 'acrylic' (dual backdrop-filter: surface blur + shadow-layer brightness) | 'auto' (acrylic unless prefers-reduced-transparency). Transparent ::backdrop; caret flips via :has(+ :popover-open).
items.docs: Props: id (required, links popovertarget), triggerLabel; snippet children. Inside a popover, a second popovertarget button closes it declaratively — still zero JS. Ships the WAAPI surface-motion kernel (lib/surface-motion.ts → @lib) — the panel's entry/exit timeline; clean consumers resolve $lib/surface-motion (Codex r1 blocking #2: the kernel was site-consumed only, breaking the install chain for every popover-dependent item).

items.name: code-card
items.title: Code card
items.description: Code display highlighting through its single default engine Shiki (lib/shiki — shiki/core + the JavaScript regex engine, no WASM): on-demand grammars and themes as separate lazy chunks, the default zero-download jixoai theme is Shiki's css-variables recipe bound to the --tok-* palette. figure+pre+code base, filename tab + header snippet slot, footer snippet slot, copyable control. Scroll law: pre is the scrollport — horizontal always (tabs stay tabs), vertical when maxHeight caps it, thin scrollbars, overscroll containment, keyboard-focusable. Code is a runtime prop; Shiki escapes it, so literal </script> is inert. Engine matrix (2026-09-06): the default install carries ONLY shiki — additional engines install as their own items (highlight-prismjs / -microlighter / -highlightjs / -sugar-high / -tree-sitter); backend prop → context default → stock shiki resolution unchanged. Language detection (highlight-lang-detector, 2026-09-07): lang='auto' (the AUTO_LANG sentinel, STRICT equality — 'AUTO'/' auto ' are ordinary langs) runs the three-ring chain langDetector prop → HIGHLIGHT_DETECT_KEY context → backend.detector, null cascades complementing, a reject terminal (plain-text fallback + warn); detection bytes load only when a card actually enters auto — a bare install carries ZERO detector code (the DLD waterfall is the highlight-lang-detector item, its wrapper highlight-detect-default).
items.docs: Props: code, lang='ts' (or 'auto' — the AUTO_LANG sentinel runs detection through the three-ring chain langDetector prop → HIGHLIGHT_DETECT_KEY context → backend.detector; the filename prop feeds the DLD's L1 tables verbatim), langDetector? (ring ① — defaultLangDetector()/betlangDetector() from the highlight-lang-detector item), theme='jixoai', filename?, copyable=true, maxHeight?; snippets header?, footer?. Based on Shiki — the highlight engine in lib/shiki is a thin on-demand facade over a stock HighlighterCore; any Shiki theme/grammar/transformer works through it (see the shiki lib item). Prerender paints the escaped plain sample; Shiki upgrades it after hydration with no layout shift. Breaking (2026-09-06): prismjs/microlighter no longer ride the install — shadcn add @jixoai/highlight-<engine> per engine; $lib/highlight/<engine> paths stay stable for installed engines.

items.name: shiki
items.title: Shiki highlighter (on-demand)
items.description: Thin Shiki integration — explicitly NOT a wrapper: a lazy singleton over shiki/core with the JavaScript regex engine (zero WASM), one dynamic import per grammar/theme (shiki/langs/*.mjs, shiki/themes/*.mjs code-split and fetched only when requested, sub-grammars auto-detected via Shiki's guessEmbeddedLanguages), and a zero-download default theme from Shiki's css-variables factory bound to --tok-*. getHighlighter() exposes the stock HighlighterCore; highlightCode(code, options) forwards Shiki's own codeToHtml options (transformers, dual themes, decorations) untouched; registerLanguage/registerTheme extend the on-demand sets with one-line imports.
items.docs: Based on Shiki (npm: shiki) — this lib adds loading strategy only, never re-interprets Shiki output. Curated grammars: typescript/tsx/javascript/jsx/svelte/html/css/scss/json/bash/markdown/yaml/vue + aliases; curated themes: github-dark/light, vitesse-dark/light, min-dark/light; anything else joins via registerLanguage/registerTheme. The jixoai theme name resolves token colors to the consumer's --tok-* CSS variables.

items.name: icon-set
items.title: Generated icon set
items.description: The named-glyph artifact behind <Icon name>: the 38 built-in lucide glyphs (arrow-right / chevron-down / x / external-link / check …) packed by @jixoai/ui-vite-plugin's icons library face into a typed IconName union + getIcon()/loadIcon()/preloadIcons() over {v,n,d} payloads. Default tier: ONE inline chunk, zero npm deps, plugin-free (synchronous getIcon, SSR paints core glyphs). Overflow tier: configs past the chunk budget (or inlineFirstChunk:false) emit lazy imports of virtual:jixoai-icons/chunk/* — that tier REQUIRES wiring jixoai({ icons: { library } }) from @jixoai/ui-vite-plugin (the documented plugin prerequisite; without it the build fails with the named sentinel error).
items.docs: GENERATED file — regenerate via the repo's gen:icons flow, never hand-edit (the GENERATED header is the contract). import { getIcon, loadIcon, preloadIcons, type IconName } from '$lib/icon-set.gen'; the default artifact carries all 38 icons in the inline chunk, so getIcon() answers synchronously and nothing needs the plugin.

items.name: form-field
items.title: Form field bridge
items.description: The faceless form-associated custom element (<jx-form-field>) that restores FormData submission to the family's custom-painted controls: formAssociated + attachInternals + setFormValue over name/value/disabled attributes, display:contents (no box, no paint, no ARIA — style stays in the component), form reset bubbling back as jx-reset and form/fieldset disable as jx-disabled. Client-only lazy registration, SSR-safe.
items.docs: Imported for its side effect by select/combobox/range/tags-input (no named exports needed at use sites). Law: a missing name, an empty value, or a disabled field contributes nothing to FormData — native control semantics.

items.name: table
items.title: Table
items.description: NativeHTML table with jixoai styling, driven by container queries on its own frame (not the viewport): full semantic thead/tbody/tfoot/th/td preserved; figure wrapper with overflow-x auto. Wide frame (>=30rem): scroll law with fit-content columns and opt-in pinned columns (data-sticky="start"|"end" on th+td stick to the scrollport behind a hairline fold mark). Narrow frame: CodePen card mode — thead folds away, td[data-label] renders muted label ::before with the value flushed right, first cell becomes the card head; stack=false keeps the scroll law at every width. Every paint routes through the --jx-table-* local token surface (surface/head/hover/hairline/rule/edge) with theme-token defaults — hover carries the --brand-hue flow, one var overrides per instance.
items.docs: Props: caption?, dense=false, stack=true, style? (passthrough landing on the frame — the color-freedom seam); snippet children (write native thead/tbody/tfoot). Consumer cell opt-ins: data-label="…" (stack-mode row label), data-sticky="start"|"end" (pinned column in scroll mode — put it on the th AND its td's). Color freedom: override --jx-table-surface/head/hover/hairline/rule/edge per instance via style or CSS.

items.name: markdown
items.title: Markdown
items.description: Markdown rendering with append-only streaming (stream-markdown-parser core — markdown-it-ts under it, CommonMark + GFM; the renderer owns the DOM, never the parser's): one keyed block per top-level AST node (${index}:${type}:${digest}; the streaming tail keys on type alone), so the frozen prefix never remounts while chunks arrive — prefix keys freeze, the tail mutates in place, remounts stay bounded to one per semantic event, and the stream's end re-parses once with final semantics. The AST maps onto first-party registry parts: blockquote → Blockquote with GitHub alert detection first (a [!NOTE|TIP|IMPORTANT|WARNING|CAUTION] marker on the quote's own first line renders tonal + label + the status hue; a half-typed marker simply renders the plain quote — the shadow-1 rule default, since 2026-09-07 every quote's left rule is an inset shadow — and keeps updating in place), heading → Heading (the em ladder migrated out of the face sheet so it scales with the ambient preset), list → List (children recurse; list_item stays a native li), paragraph → P and inline marks → the text family (Strong/Em/Del/Mark/Ins/Sub/Sup — one word is prop value, sugar name, and HTML element), link → Link (absolute http(s) opens externally), inline_code → InlineCode riding the component's lang='auto' default (detection is sync fingerprints, zero-download; the grammar highlight is the async in-place upgrade through the engine seam — SSR plain, zero layout shift), thematic_break → Separator behind a neutral carrier div, code_block → CodeCard (partial code + loading state mid-fence, generation-guard repaint is CodeCard's own path), table → a semantically neutral div[data-kind=table] wrapping Table with generated thead/tbody, td[data-label] row labels and per-column align. Box-owning block roots escape the jx-pure Tier-0 prose face (no-jx-pure on Blockquote/Heading/List roots and the InlineCode chip, Separator's carrier div) so the face stops double-painting them; face-composing inline members never escape (P, the marks, Link — an inline escape would virally descope the code chips and nested marks a link legitimately contains). Task checkboxes stay native disabled inputs (the jx-pure bare-checkbox face paints them); image stays the sanitized native img. The root mounts the face class; the sheet itself is the app-level import, imported once from the site css the way jixoai.css is — never a forked copy of the face laws, never a second component-level import that would double-bundle it. Security floor: html:false + the renderer's escaped-literal law (raw markup survives as text, zero {@html} in the default map), the factory validateLink demotes unsafe schemes at parse time, image src passes the bitmap-data-URL sanitizer (SVG and other data schemes omit the img entirely). The components override seam is trusted application code — the same trust level as any component the app renders by hand. The component is a pure function of (source, streaming): server render and client hydration parse the same snapshot (the SSR snapshot law); data-jx-markdown-streaming + the terminal cursor stamp the root only while streaming. HTML is markdown spelled differently (2026-09-07): whitelisted tags (<b>, <strong>, <details>/<summary>, <code>, <kbd>, <a>, <hr>…) route onto the SAME components as their markdown spellings; every other tag stays escaped literal text.

items.name: blockquote
items.title: Blockquote
items.description: The reading-content quote/admonition surface: the semantic body IS the native <blockquote> (cite renders the MDN attribution posture — footer > cite — never an element swap), on the alert-shaped two-rung ladder: outline (own) transparent ground + 1px left rule + muted body (the classic GitHub/Tailwind quote), tonal the alert tonal recipe verbatim (12% tinted ground, 45% border, rounded box — the callout/Notion posture). The rule channel (2026-09-07, typography-context-and-parts): rule (shadow|border, own shadow — the inset standard the Owner cited: command-item's shadow-[inset_2px_0_0_var(--primary)], the elevation grammar's WELL tier, kbd's --shadow-engrave lineage) × ruleSize (the literal 1|4|8 px ladder, own 1 — the Owner's explicit enumeration, not a derived scale); the rule color rides the rung's OWN border-color declaration (one hue source — jx-hue-* retunes ground+box+rule together), ONE shadow utility per root, outline in shadow mode emits no border at all (the shadow carries the rule), tonal keeps its box border plus the shadow rule so tonal+shadow-1 is a deliberate near-no-op (axis uniformity over special-casing), and the paddings stay FIXED across channels and sizes (border consumes geometry, shadow doesn't — paint never moves geometry). Forced colors: shadow modes re-materialize as an Npx CanvasText border; border modes keep the rung degradation. Availability is FROZEN at two rungs: quote readability excludes fill AND ghost — ghost is interactive-chrome vocabulary (rest-transparent, hover-tonal) which a static quote misuses; the borderless manuscript indent is a future STRUCTURAL axis, never a paint rung. label renders the alert title-row form, icon lands inline-start of it (bring your own glyph), hue rides injection through jx-hue-* class utilities (the markdown map's GitHub alerts land here as tonal + label + hue). The root stamps NO font-size — the ambient scale flows by inheritance (the typography trio law); the markdown default map mounts it with no-jx-pure (the box-owning block escape).

items.name: list

The marker vocabulary (2026-09-07, typography-context-and-parts): marker disc|circle|square|decimal|alpha|roman|none — element-agnostic frozen set, lowercase only (upper = the escape hatch); omitted keeps the per-element platform default (decimal on ol, disc on ul — today's byte-parity), explicit overrides, and circle/square ride the arbitrary [list-style:] form (they silently no-op as core utilities under TW 4.2.1); marker ink stays the muted law, marker size/spacing deliberately absent (ambient scale + the no-margins law), none keeps the structural ps-6. This is NOT list-item — that item is the antd/F7 settings-row system (ItemGroup frames, media/end lanes, five control adapters); this one styles the LIST, never the row, and the markdown map composes it with native <li> children (list_item stays bare so the element-based rhythm selectors and the container-inner sibling stack keep matching). items.name: prose
items.title: Prose
items.description: The reading region provider: <Prose size leading family ink gradient ground align indent initialLetter wrap hyphens> renders div.jx-pure[data-jx-prose] — NOT <Typography>, that word is markdown's live user-facing vocabulary (<Markdown typography="relaxed">); two concepts under one name is documentation debt forever. The provider resolves the ELEVEN frozen v1 knobs through ProseDefaults (every one an absentSlot — ABSENCE IS THE STATE: an unset knob emits nothing, stamps nothing, and the ambient channel — an outer prose region's declarations/vars, or no opinion at all — keeps flowing; nested regions inherit every knob they do not set, nearest setter wins) and applies the plugin chain AT THE PROVIDER (applyTypoScope, read inside the $derived so medium-gated filters re-run; a print-medium plugin can strip gradient/ground before CSS sees them) before the PURE resolver emits the two channels: declarations (the inheritance lane — font-size/family/color/text-align/text-wrap/hyphens/background-color) + the --jx-ty-* var mirrors (documented for app-side css reads) + presence hooks (data-jx-ty-leading/-indent/-initial, data-jx-ty-ink="gradient" — presence-gated because an ungated var(--jx-ty-leading, inherit) rule at (0,2,0) would fire always and break the face's p{1.6} for every non-prose region). The element lanes live in prose.css, the scope-owned residue sheet, every rule at (0,2,0): the leading un-short-circuit generalization and the indent lane (P-only — headings never inherit a first-line indent), the drop cap in BOTH arms (@supports initial-letter modern path + the float ::first-letter fallback — a browser-class-dependent drop cap reads as a bug; suppresses indent on the same P; keeps printing on paper, the manuscript posture), and the FILL-ONLY gradient lane (background-clip:text + -webkit-text-fill-color, NEVER color:transparent — currentcolor on a mark would resolve to the inherited transparent and vanish; marks restore solid by element rule; --jx-ty-ink carries only color tokens so Heading's var-fallback utility never sees an invalid-at-computed-value-time var; --jx-ty-ink-solid ships for plugin and print reads; @media print and forced-colors restores live in the same sheet — the paged.js clone never re-runs the provider). SOVEREIGNTY by cascade, zero JS masking: every residue rule beats the face element rules and LOSES to the markdown sheet's §2a (0,2,1) inside [data-jx-markdown] — an outer <Prose size leading> can never fight <Markdown typography=…>; ink/flow knobs pass through; chrome stays unaffected BY CASCADE (element-level declarations beat an inherited wrapper color); code/kbd stay mono under family (face B1 element rules); prose stamps no density (the trio's own naming argument). The context pair ships in the typography lib (provideTypography/getTypographyScope, getter-endorsed — a provider flip re-derives future consumers in the same frame).

(number; P-only lane, headings keep 1.25), family? ('sans'|'mono'|'serif' → the theme --font-* tokens — 'serif' NEEDS the theme to define --font-serif, documented not assumed — or a raw font-family value; code/kbd keep their mono law), ink? ('default'|'muted'|'primary'|'destructive' → the four foreground tokens, or raw color; links keep primary, the face B2 recorded exception), gradient? ({from,to,angle?} composes a linear-gradient — numeric angle → degrees, default 180deg — or a raw CSS image value; fill-only), ground? ('background'|'card'|'popover'|'muted'|'secondary'|'accent'|'transparent' or raw; Mark's own highlight law untouched), align? ('start'|'center'|'end'|'justify'; justify pairs with hyphens), indent? (CssLength, P-only; '2em' = 中文稿纸惯例), initialLetter? (2|3|4|5; both arms; suppresses indent on the same P), wrap? ('pretty' for prose, 'balance' for heading scopes, 'stable'), hyphens? items.docs: Props: page, pageCount, href (template fn), label?, siblings? (1), prevLabel?/nextLabel?. Module export: pageWindow(page, pageCount, siblings).

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown menu
items.description: The ARIA menu pattern on the popover laws: popover=auto panel (light dismiss, Escape, top layer native) + CSS Anchor Positioning, roving item focus, type-ahead. Floating-surface law: ::after shadow layer + @starting-style entry; variant solid|acrylic|auto.
items.docs: Root props: id, triggerLabel?, placement? ('bottom-end'), trigger? (custom snippet), panelClass?, onToggle?. Item props: destructive?, plus <button> passthrough; separators are plain <hr>, labels plain markup.

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.description: The breadcrumb as composed shadcn anatomy: List/Item/Link(child)/Page/Separator(children glyph override)/Ellipsis parts. Collapse is an OPT-IN part (BreadcrumbCollapse wraps the middle items; its ellipsis links to the first hidden page). Dropdown is the sibling-jump part (BreadcrumbDropdown: click opens a menu of peer destinations — REAL anchor entries, current page marked, selection dismisses and navigates). No width magic in Root.
items.docs: Props: crumbs ({label, href}[], last = current page), label?, collapse? (max visible before the middle folds, 0 = never). Dropdown: label, items ({label, href}[]), current? (href marked aria-current=page).

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: The keyboard-input glyph: a native <kbd> — the element whose entire meaning is 'this is keyboard input' — with the jixoai chip paint (1px border, shadow-2xs, mono). Deliberately no key-parsing or platform detection: compose by hand (<Kbd>⌘</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>).
items.docs: Props: any <kbd> attribute passthrough; children = the key label.

items.name: inline-code
items.title: Inline code
items.description: The inline source-code chip: a native <code> in the variant grammar's fused/tonal/outline ladder (fused default — the backdrop-fusion band: transparent ground + a backdrop contrast filter over whatever sits behind, auto-adaptive across themes and patterned grounds with zero color tokens; the fusion IS the frame, forced-colors repaints it CanvasText; tonal keeps the neutral [--jx-tonal:…] / jx-hue-* injection seam, consumers win from either layer). Geometry: radius rides the density ladder token --jx-chip-radius (2xs/xs/sm 2px, default 4px, lg 8px — not the global --radius), padding-inline = radius + fontSize × (lineHeight − 1) / 2 (token calc by default; explicit fontSize/lineHeight fold the excess). Highlighting rides the engine seam (backend prop → HIGHLIGHT_KEY context → the stock microlighter RANGE engine — zero markup, plain text stays copyable; a CSS.highlights pre-gate degrades to plain text silently where the API is missing, and print loses ranges by the documented freeze limitation). lang='auto' runs the zero-download fingerprint heuristic (INLINE_LANGS/detectInlineLang exported); the six text modifiers (lineHeight/weight/italic/tracking/family/fontSize) resolve through the shared @jixoai/text kernel.
items.docs: Props: variant='fused' ('fused'|'tonal'|'outline'), lang='auto', backend? (HighlightBackend — prop → HIGHLIGHT_KEY context → stock microlighter), lineHeight?/weight?/italic?/tracking?/family?/fontSize? (the shared text-modifier kernel; fontSize/lineHeight also feed the padding calc), density?, class?; rest flow to the native <code>. Module exports INLINE_LANGS + detectInlineLang.

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: The variant grammar's compact activation: the badge's font-nav uppercase micro-label voice on the control-scale hit lane — the ROOT carries min-block-size var(--jx-hit) (~44px at default density), not a 20px badge. Four ladder rungs consumed as global tokens: fill (solid ground + same-hue border), tonal (12%/45% tint recipe, default), outline (structural border + 8% hover overlay), ghost (transparent rest, tonal hover, shadowless press); semantic hue is injected (jx-hue-error — the @utility intent layer), never named. Button/anchor duality (external hrefs open a new tab with noreferrer), slotStart/slotEnd data-icon lanes, square/pill silhouette, press-button's effect builders passed through with ripple() as the default ink (null disables); explicit forced-colors degradation (ButtonFace/ButtonText, Canvas/CanvasText, ghost transparent/ButtonFace hover, 2px Highlight focus never removed).
items.docs: Props: density?, variant? ('fill'|'tonal'|'outline'|'ghost', default 'tonal'), shape? ('square'|'pill'), effect? (PressEffect | null — default ripple(), null disables), href?, external?, onclick?, type?, ariaLabel?, class?, slotStart?/slotEnd? (Snippet), children (required). Imports the effect builders, ripple runtime and effect-layer css from @ui/press-button.

items.name: link
items.title: Link
items.description: The typographic link: a native <a> carrying the prose face's non-nav lane as its own utilities (primary ink, 4px underline offset, hover underline) so it stands alone outside any jx-pure scope — and inside one the values coincide with the face's own channels (same property, same token, deterministic no-op). External detection is pattern-based, not origin-based (ANY absolute http(s) href is external; no window.location semantics dragged into SSR): external links open a new tab with rel=noreferrer (the fleet convention — doc-link and PressButton both ship bare noreferrer; modern browsers imply noopener from it). The suffix-icon lane (2026-09-07, typography-context-and-parts): tri-state icon — undefined paints the default externalLink glyph IFF external (an inline-core name answering getIcon synchronously, SSR paints it, hydration matches, no flash), null turns the lane OFF, a snippet renders custom content; the lane is an aria-hidden data-jx-link-icon span inside the anchor after the children (em-sized 0.8em, rides any ambient scale), and internal links never carry it. Hook: data-jx-link="external"|"internal" — the separator's data-orientation form. href/title and the external pair land AFTER the spread (the separator law): they are the component's contract, not overridable through rest props.
items.docs: Props: href (required — an absolute http(s) href makes the link external: target=_blank + rel=noreferrer), title? (advisory passthrough), icon? (Snippet | null — the suffix-icon lane, tri-state: undefined → the default externalLink glyph shown IFF external; null → the lane off; a snippet → custom glyph content), children, class plus every anchor attribute passthrough. Hooks: data-jx-link={external ? 'external' : 'internal'} + data-jx-link-icon on the lane span. No Defaults file — external-ness derives from href.

items.name: text
items.title: Text
items.description:
The reading-content family the Owner designed: base renders

by default (the Chakra -is-a-paragraph precedent) and mark switches the element and paint — ONE vocabulary where the prop value, the sugar name, and the HTML element are the same word: p (no utilities; face-composing), strong ( font-semibold — the GitHub/Tailwind Typography 600 settle, a recorded override of the face's 700), em ( italic), del ( line-through), mark ( highlight ground + the 0.05em/0.25em padding box mirroring the face's mark so standalone and in-face agree; forced colors drop to the Highlight pair), ins ( underline), sub/sup (/ — the UA baseline shift is the law). mark is a LITERAL slot (defineLiteralSlot, own 'p' — the kbd variant precedent): element vocabulary, never prominence, never zone-ambient. The eight Raw sugars (P Strong Em Del Mark Ins Sub Sup) are re-exported from the base's module script and the barrel — one vocabulary, two ergonomic forms, zero behavioral difference. FACE-COMPOSING: no member escapes no-jx-pure (an inline escape would virally descope the code chips and nested marks a link legitimately contains); the root stamps NO font-size — the ambient scale flows by inheritance.
items.docs: Props: mark? ('p' default | 'strong' | 'em' | 'del' | 'mark' | 'ins' | 'sub' | 'sup' — the element vocabulary; a literal slot, own 'p', never zone-ambient), children, class plus the chosen element's attribute passthrough. Raw sugars: import Text, { P, Strong, Em, Del, Mark, Ins, Sub, Sup } from '@ui/text' — Text mark="x" ≡ the x sugar (same element, same data-jx-text hook, same class-merge order). Hook: data-jx-text={form}.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Two seams, per the design ruling: createToastStore() (framework-free state + lifecycle — push/dismiss/subscribe, per-toast expiry with hover/focus pause, duration 0 = sticky, no module singleton so SSR stays clean; variant grammar: variant 'outline'|'tonal' + the hue-injection seam, e.g. class 'jx-hue-error' for failed statuses (the @utility intent layer)) and ToastViewport (mount once in the root layout: fixed corner stack, max visible with older queued, per-item live regions — role=status polite / role=alert assertive, dismiss buttons, entry/exit frames; the ladder paints over the floating popover ground with explicit forced-colors degradation).
items.docs: const toast = createToastStore(); <ToastViewport store={toast} /> … toast.api.push({ title, description?, variant? 'outline'|'tonal', material?, effect?, countdown?, duration?, assertive?, expandable?, swipeDirections? }). toast-v2/R3: nine float slots via pos (default right-bottom), the stack collapses with depth and expands on hover/touch (expand prop pins it; a touch tap lifts stickily until an outside tap), swipe dismisses toward the slot’s nearest screen edges (48px / 0.11 px·ms), a hidden page freezes every clock (pauseAll/resumeAll), and expandable toasts morph into a dialog through a view transition.

items.name: system-dialog
items.title: System dialog
items.description: The confirmation dialog as a composed family (shadcn-shaped on the native <dialog>): Root (bind:open/onconfirm) + Trigger/Content/Title/Description/Actions/Action(variant: fill with the destructive pair injected by default | tonal | outline)/Cancel — focus lands on Cancel (the safe default), Escape cancels, confirm runs then closes. No Overlay/Portal parts (the dialog element IS the overlay) — recorded divergence.
items.docs: Props: title, description (both required), open ($bindable), confirmLabel, confirmTone? ('destructive' default | 'primary'), onconfirm?, cancelLabel?, children? (extra body).

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: The side drawer as a dialog POSITIONING variant (not a second state machine): showModal(), side docking + slide along the docked axis, generation-token close. Floating-surface law: ::after shadow layer + variant solid|acrylic|auto riding on top of the slide; --scrim backdrop; the slide keeps the sheet's own 200ms timing (declared exception to the 120ms dialog default).
items.docs: Props: open ($bindable), title, side? ('right' default), size? (CSS length, 24rem default), header?/footer? snippets, children.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover card
items.description: The rich interactive cousin of tooltip: popover=manual panel, close grace spans the panel, CSS anchoring. Floating-surface law: ::after shadow layer + @starting-style entry; variant solid|acrylic|auto.
items.docs: Props: trigger (snippet), children (the card), placement? ('bottom' default), openDelay? (300), closeDelay? (200).

items.name: input-otp
items.title: Input OTP
items.description: The one-time-code field: N single-character inputs with the mechanics a raw stack lacks — auto-advance, backstep on backspace, paste distributing across slots, focus landing on the first empty slot (entering from outside only). Submits ONE joined value through the jx-form-field ElementInternals bridge (partial codes submit empty, never a partial lie).
items.docs: Props: name?, length? (6), value ($bindable), numeric? (true), label?, error?, disabled?. Two-way slot/value sync is untracked on the slots side — slot mutations can never be re-synced against stale value. Requires the form-field bridge item (installed as its dependency).

items.name: toggle-group
items.title: Toggle group
items.description: The joined segment row of NATIVE inputs: single = label>input[type=radio] under one name (native arrow-walk + one tab stop + exclusivity; re-press does NOT clear — an explicit none item is the pattern), multiple = checkboxes submitting one FormData entry per press (getAll on the server). DOM checked is the uncontrolled truth; value is the projection; form.reset() re-syncs. The paint law is the shared Part A .jx-tgroup class from @jixoai/jx-native-contract (never redefined here); the jx-form-field bridge is retired for this family.
items.docs: Props: name (REQUIRED for type=single — radio grouping and arrow-walking are name-scoped; optional for multiple), type ('single'|'multiple'), value ($bindable string|string[]), label (required a11y name), required (single mode only — forwards to every input), disabled, density, onValueChange ((value) => void; native event forwarding rides the spread alongside, never instead). NATIVE contract: single rides label>input[type=radio] (arrow-walk, ONE tab stop, no re-press clear — an explicit none item is the optional-empty pattern); multiple rides checkboxes — FormData carries one entry per active value in DOM order (server reads getAll); the jx-form-field bridge is GONE. DOM checked is the uncontrolled truth; form.reset() re-syncs the projection via the reset event. The paint law is the shared Part A .jx-tgroup class (@jixoai/jx-native-contract); segments compose as ToggleGroupItem parts (label.jx-tgroup-item > input + span.jx-tgroup-content, slotStart/slotEnd snippets, no interactive descendants inside the label).

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.description: W3C-first: a carousel IS a scrolled region — CSS scroll-snap does the paging, native scrolling does the motion (momentum, keyboard when focused). JS only READS the position (rAF-throttled) to keep the dots honest. No slide cloning, no virtual window: slides are ordinary direct children of the track. Dots page; arrows page; the active dot follows the nearest snap slide.
items.docs: Props: label?, slideWidth? ('100%' one-at-a-time; '80%' for peeking), dots?, prevLabel/nextLabel?, children = the slides (any elements).

items.name: command
items.title: Command palette
items.description: The command palette as a composed cmdk-style family: Input/List/Empty/Group/Item parts; items SELF-MATCH ({label, keywords} vs query through the match inclusion predicate — filtering hides, NEVER reorders; authored tree order is the walk order). hint is a snippet (kbd glyph content); disabled items render but never enter the walk, never become activedescendant, never fire on Enter. Groups self-hide and the empty state reveals via CSS :has.
items.docs: Props: items (CommandItem[]), open ($bindable), onopenchange?, onselect? (single execution path — no dual run()), closeOnSelect? (true), placeholder?, label?, hotkey? (false — opt-in), filter? (pure function, default rankCommandItems export).

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: Navigation menu
items.description: The site-nav bar as a composed family riding the Popover primitive: declarative popovertarget wire, light dismiss, one-at-a-time; Item/Trigger/Panel/Link parts; the mega-grid is authored INSIDE the panel by the consumer. Viewport/Indicator are recorded divergences (per-panel CSS anchoring replaces the Radix shared viewport). OPTIONAL NavigationMenuIndicator part: the sliding-active indicator with two motion laws — motion="navigation" stamps a view-transition-name for page-level View Transition morphs (inert without transitions; same-document moves animate via WAAPI), motion="waapi" is the pure Web Animations path for apps without View Transitions.
items.docs: Props: items ({id,label,href?,current?,hasPanel?}[]), label?, panel? (snippet [item]), variant? ('auto' | 'solid' | 'acrylic'). The panel rides the popover primitive's motion kernel; open state mirrors the native toggle seam only. Indicator (optional part): motion ('navigation'|'waapi'), name (view-transition-name), duration.

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.description: The application menu bar as a composed family (Radix Menubar shape): Item owns the id + anchor (Trigger/Panel derive their ids — the ID derivation protocol), Panel is a popover=manual role=menu registering handles at init; ←/→ glide, ↓/↑/Enter open, per-panel motion kernels, DOM-scoped panel walks (nested menus never leak); MenubarMenuItem closes-and-restores on select.
items.docs: Props: items ({id,label}[]), label?, panel (snippet [item] — bring buttons/links with role=menuitem).

items.name: popconfirm
items.title: Popconfirm
items.description: The light confirm bubble (NOT an alertdialog): trigger = children; panel content/actions open via content/actions snippets with the current rendering as defaults. Light dismiss = cancel.
items.docs: Props: title (required), description?, onconfirm?, oncancel?, confirmLabel/cancelLabel?, confirmTone? ('destructive' default), placement? ('top'). children = the trigger; the wrapper auto-wires the first button as popovertarget.

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty
items.description: The no-data state of the eight-state machine — nothing more (error/loading/404 are alert/result surfaces). A figure: terminal illustration slot (default: the empty directory listing), title, description, actions snippet. Pure composition, zero JS.
items.docs: Props: title (required), description?, illustration? (snippet), actions? (snippet). The illustration slot is decorative by contract (aria-hidden) — informational art belongs in the body.

items.name: descriptions
items.title: Descriptions
items.description: The enterprise detail view as a composed dl: Descriptions (columns/bordered HOW-props) + DescriptionsItem (term → dt, children → dd — rich cells are just children; childless items render the em dash).
items.docs: Props: items ({term, value?}[]), columns? (1-4, default 1), bordered?, value? (per-item rich cell snippet).

items.name: steps
items.title: Steps
items.description: The wizard progress as a composed family: a nine-word state vocabulary (auto trio + middle pending, success/error/hint/emphasis/disabled) overrides the derived done/current/todo comparison when stated explicitly. The done Indicator becomes the button (a link back) when onclick is given; the current step is aria-current=step; future steps are inert spans. CSS connector; check glyph on done; the Separator self-hides on the last item.
items.docs: Props: steps ({title, description?}[]), current (0-based), onstepclick? (fires for completed steps).

items.name: spin
items.title: Spin
items.description: The loading indicator, terminal voice: a bracket cursor cycling [/ — \ |]. role=status (polite by construction). Bare = inline glyph; wrapping = aria-busy container where the scrim OWNS pointer events (never a visual mask with live hit areas beneath — loading and disabled are different states).
items.docs: Props: label? ('loading'), children? (wrapping posture when given). reduced-motion freezes to the first frame.

items.name: statistic
items.title: Statistic
items.description: The metric readout: micro-label over a big tabular-nums value with prefix/suffix snippets and a text-glyph trend (▲ primary / ▼ destructive). The component never guesses what 'good' means for your metric — compose your own semantics through the snippets.
items.docs: Props: title (required), value (string|number — formatting is yours), prefix?/suffix? (snippets), trend? ('up'|'down').

items.name: timeline
items.title: Timeline
items.description: The activity stream rebuilt as a 5-lane grid engine: direction ltr/revert/interlaced, axis vertical/horizontal, per-node 9-grid dots (8 logical slots + center dot via grid+subgrid), the line authored-free by default and replaceable through a line(i) snippet, preset line components (Dashed, animated Beam), scroll- and view-driven animations (@supports-gated, reduced-motion-safe). timeline-connector is retired — the line IS grid tracks.
items.docs: Timeline props: axis ('vertical'|'horizontal'), direction ('ltr'|'revert'|'interlaced'), animation ('none'|'view'|'scroll'). TimelineDot: 8 logical snippet slots (blockStart/inlineStart/inlineEnd/blockEnd and the four corners) + center dot, variant square/round/ring. Line presets: TimelineLineDashed, TimelineLineBeam; or replace wholesale with a line(i) snippet.

items.name: result
items.title: Result
items.description: The page-level outcome of an operation — deliberately THIN: status glyph + title + description + actions, no 403/404 routing logic, no illustration system (bring your own icon snippet). Success paints through the brand voice (no green in this language); error destructive. empty ≠ result: no-data vs operation-outcome stay different components.
items.docs: Props: status? ('success'|'error'|'warning'|'info'), title (required), description?, icon? (snippet), actions? (snippet). The icon slot is decorative by contract (aria-hidden).

items.name: transfer
items.title: Transfer
items.description: The two-panel selector: each side is a real fieldset of real checkboxes (native multi-select semantics), the middle buttons batch-move every checked row, and per-panel search filters by label. value ($bindable) is the TARGET list — moving never mutates options; selection is transient and clears after each move; disabled rows render but never move.
items.docs: Props: options ({value,label,disabled?}[]), value ($bindable string[]), name? (bridge: target values submit as multi-entry FormData), sourceTitle/targetTitle?, searchPlaceholder?, onchange?.

items.name: cascader
items.title: Cascader
items.description: The cascade selector, chain-of-selects route (the ruled default): N plain <select> elements, each listing the children of the previous pick — native option semantics, native keyboard, native mobile pickers, zero panels. The joined PATH submits through the jx-form-field bridge (separator '/', default); a partial path submits '' (the input-otp law). The antd multi-column search panel is the documented upgrade route.
items.docs: Props: options (CascaderOption tree), name?, value ($bindable string[]), separator?, disabled?, label?, placeholder?.

items.name: image
items.title: Image
items.description: The general-purpose picture on avatar's proven laws: native , lazy, async-decoded, REQUIRED intrinsic width/height (the no-CLS contract), alt semantics (text by default, '' opts decorative), and a failure fallback with src-change reset + composed onerror. Lightbox/preview is deliberately a dialog recipe, not built in.
items.docs: Props: alt (required), width/height (required intrinsic), fallback? (snippet), plus passthrough.

items.name: float-button
items.title: Float button
items.description: The floating action button: a fixed corner button in two idioms — plain (a lone action, e.g. back-to-top) and menu (children + actions snippet: the button toggles a popover=auto stack above it, native light dismiss). Corner is a prop, not a wrapper — the consumer's layout is never touched. Press law (.jx-press) at float scale (--shadow rest, --shadow-md hover). The menu panel rides the floating-surface law: ::after shadow layer (semi-transparent black/white) + @starting-style entry; variant='solid' | 'acrylic' | 'auto' (acrylic falls back to solid under prefers-reduced-transparency; the button itself keeps the press law).
items.docs: Props: label (required — icon-only buttons must say themselves), corner? ('bottom-right' default), onclick? (plain), actions? (snippet, menu idiom), children (icon/glyph). Menu idiom: the actions snippet must bring real buttons/links carrying role=menuitem (the walk contract is theirs).

items.name: badge-indicator
items.title: Badge indicator
items.description: antd Badge's live half — the count/dot overlay riding a corner of its child (avatar, icon, tab): dot is presence without a number; count caps at overflow (99+ default); count=0 hides honestly (zero unread IS no badge) unless showZero. Standalone (no children) renders an inline chip.
items.docs: Props: dot?, count?, overflow? (99), showZero?, label? (required name in dot mode), children? (the host element).

items.name: anchor
items.title: Anchor
items.description: The in-page rail as a composed family: AnchorItem children are the targets (DOM-delegated scrollspy — no registration); the pick paints aria-current=location; offset drives the sticky-header pick line; capture-phase scroll listening covers inner scrollers.
items.docs: Props: items ({href:'#id', label}[]), label?, offset? (96 — the pick line, for sticky headers).

items.name: tour
items.title: Tour
items.description: The spotlight tour: steps carry targets (behavior domain, driver.js precedent); the card opens via the card(api) snippet ({index, total, step, next, prev, skip}) with the zero-config default card when absent. Spotlight, focus and step lifecycle unchanged.
items.docs: Props: steps ({target: selector | resolver, title, description?}[]), open ($bindable), startAt?, onfinish?(stoppedAtIndex), onstep?, nextLabel/prevLabel/skipLabel?.

items.name: ghostty-vt
items.title: ghostty-vt wasm binding
items.description: Framework-free WebAssembly binding for libghostty-vt with an xterm.js-convention Terminal facade: init() loads the shared wasm core, new Terminal({cols, rows, cursorBlink, cursorStyle}) speaks write/writeln/paste/resize/reset/clear/scrollLines, disposable onData/onResize, getSelection/hasSelection/clearSelection, and renderer-facing extensions (dirtyRows, readCursor, handleKey). Under the facade the raw ABI core stays first-class: every struct offset, enum value and cell bit parsed at load time from ghostty_type_json() — zero hardcoded offsets, immune to nightly ABI drift. Cursor (DECSCUSR + OSC 12 color), drag/word/line selection gestures, paste gate, base64 snapshots, typed GhosttyVTError.
items.docs: await init({ url }) from the virtual:jixoai-ghostty module (or pass a core for test isolation). const term = new Terminal(); term.write(ptyBytes); term.onData(s => sendToPty(s)); paint from term.dirtyRows() + term.readCursor(); keys via term.handleKey(KeyboardEvent); selection via getSelection(). xterm.js users: the facade maps 1:1 to the API you know; dirtyRows/readCursor are the renderer extensions.

items.name: highlight
items.title: Pluggable highlight backends (core contract)
items.description: The engine-agnostic CONTRACT of the highlight matrix (highlight-engine-matrix, 2026-09-06): the HighlightBackend interface (markup vs range output models), the zero-dependency context seam (HIGHLIGHT_KEY via plain getContext — the density precedent), and the two runtime helpers every factory shares (requestedLang / canonicalLang) — PLUS the language-detection contract (highlight-lang-detector, 2026-09-07): the LanguageDetector interface + the AUTO_LANG sentinel (lang-detector.ts — STRICT equality, 'AUTO'/' auto ' are ordinary langs) and the second zero-dependency seam HIGHLIGHT_DETECT_KEY (context-key.ts — every write path stores the same { detector } adapter shape). ZERO npm dependencies and ZERO engine imports ride this item — engines install as their own items (highlight-shiki / -prismjs / -microlighter / -highlightjs / -sugar-high / -tree-sitter), the DLD waterfall as highlight-lang-detector; the app side owns the default via the seam or a per-instance backend prop.
items.docs: import type { HighlightBackend } from '$lib/highlight/backend' — one interface, two output models: markup backends write token spans into the element (survive the print freeze), range backends register CSS Custom Highlight ranges (zero markup; degrade on paper). Engine factories live in their own items; the shipped context seam is context-key.ts only (kernel wiring stays app-side). The detection half rides the same contract files: AUTO_LANG + LanguageDetector from '$lib/highlight/lang-detector', the HIGHLIGHT_DETECT_KEY seam from '$lib/highlight/context-key' (the DLD waterfall itself is the highlight-lang-detector item).

items.name: highlight-shiki
items.title: Shiki highlight backend
items.description: The DEFAULT engine of the matrix (highlight-engine-matrix, 2026-09-06): the shiki() backend factory over lib/shiki — a thin adapter with zero new downloads, plus the per-instance langs allowlist (shiki({ langs: [...] }) restricts an instance without touching the shared facade registry; omitted = the full curated set). Markup output; the pre editor-colors ride-along and the plain-structure guard carry over from highlight-backend-pluggable (2026-09-02). code-card pins this engine as its only default; the stock DEFAULT_SHIKI_BACKEND singleton is the no-provider fallback.
items.docs: import { shiki, DEFAULT_SHIKI_BACKEND } from '$lib/highlight/shiki' — <CodeCard backend={shiki()}>; shiki({ langs: ['ts', 'bash'] }) slims the instance; the jixoai default theme is the zero-download --tok-* css-variables recipe (see the shiki lib item).

items.name: highlight-prismjs
items.title: Prism.js highlight backend
items.description: The prismjs() backend factory as its own item (highlight-engine-matrix, 2026-09-06): lazy manual-mode core, dependency-ordered grammar chains, lazy stock theme stylesheets, and the per-instance langs allowlist (prismjs({ langs: [...] }); omitted = the full curated set minus what prismjs 1.30 no longer ships — svelte/vue). Markup output (survives print); one active theme per document (last requested wins) is Prism's own model.
items.docs: import { prismjs } from '$lib/highlight/prismjs' — <CodeCard backend={prismjs()}>; prismjs({ langs: ['css'] }) slims the instance; unknown ids reject with a hint and the card falls back to plain text.

items.name: highlight-microlighter
items.title: MicroLighter highlight backend
items.description: The microLighter() backend factory as its own item (highlight-engine-matrix, 2026-09-06): the RANGE output model — zero markup, tokens registered as CSS Custom Highlight API ranges over the plain text node, painted by a data-syntax-theme scoped stylesheet. Feature-gated (browsers without the API reject before touching the DOM); whole-document rescan per paint (its global registry law); known, test-locked limitation: ranges do not survive the print freeze — pin a markup backend for paper. No langs option: microlighter ships one all-in TextMate set (the spec's engine exemption).
items.docs: import { microLighter, DEFAULT_MICROLIGHTER_BACKEND } from '$lib/highlight/microlighter' — <CodeCard backend={microLighter()}>; inline-code pins this engine as its stock default (the prop → context → DEFAULT_MICROLIGHTER_BACKEND singleton chain, mirroring code-card's shiki posture); the default theme is the item-local jixoai bridge (--syntax-* onto the surface's --tok-token-* palette, site-mode adaptive, zero light-dark() — the chip carries the palette itself, so the bridge resolves without a card); named themes are microlighter package stylesheet ids verbatim (min, github, dracula… — they resolve light-dark() against the OS color-scheme: hosts whose mode diverges pin pre[data-syntax-theme] color-scheme, see the docs site's app.css). Vite hosts: the engine loads grammars via runtime-templated relative imports and swallows misses silently — dev needs optimizeDeps: { exclude: ['microlighter'] }, a build must emit node_modules/microlighter/dist/grammars/*.js next to the engine chunk (see the file header's bundler contract; the docs site's vite.config.ts is the reference). Scans are rAF-coalesced document-wide (one highlightAll per frame — the global registry law). Theme hosts: microlighter themes resolve light-dark() against the OS color-scheme, not your site's mode — pin `pre[data-syntax-theme]` color-scheme to your dark-class state (the docs site's app.css is the reference).

items.name: highlight-highlightjs
items.title: highlight.js backend
items.description: The highlightJs() backend factory (highlight-engine-matrix, 2026-09-06): highlight.js/lib/core (zero-language kernel) + per-language on-demand registration — the flagship size-slimming channel of the matrix (core + your langs at RUNTIME — unselected grammars never import or fetch; vs the main-entry full bundle). Curated set: typescript/javascript/xml/css/scss/json/bash/markdown/yaml + aliases; highlight.js 11 ships NO tsx/jsx/svelte/vue — those reject with a 'use the shiki backend' hint. Language boundaries are enforced against THIS curated table, never the engine's self-registered aliases (typescript self-reports a tsx alias — measured, guarded). Markup output; the jixoai default theme is an item-shipped stylesheet binding the measured 41-class vocabulary to --tok-token-* (34 rules, zero download, shiki-parity posture). Ships the engine-borne DETECTOR slot (highlight-lang-detector D7, 2026-09-07): highlightAuto over EXACTLY the instance's candidate set — registered into a PRIVATE newInstance() registry (the shared kernel never narrows; sibling factories mutually invisible), langs omitted = the full curated pool, langs:[] = null (never a guess), hits reported under canonical ids with source 'engine' and no confidence, misses and load failures null to the cascade.
items.docs: import { highlightJs } from '$lib/highlight/highlight-js' — <CodeCard backend={highlightJs()}>; highlightJs({ langs: ['ts', 'bash'] }) registers only those languages; unknown/absent languages reject with a hint and the card falls back to plain text. Every instance also answers lang='auto' through its built-in detector (highlightAuto over exactly the instance's langs — the card's ring ③; the DLD waterfall is the standalone item).

items.name: highlight-sugar-high

Its emitted spans carry class + unresolved var(--sh-*) references with NO stylesheet in the package, so the jixoai default theme is an item-shipped variable-level mapping (--sh-* → --tok-token-*), lazily applied. Zero options by exemption: the all-in-one set IS the minimal distribution (per-language splitting is not its model). tsx rejects with a 'use the shiki backend' hint (frozen contract; the engine's own tsx→typescript alias is documented in the factory header).

items.name: highlight-tree-sitter
items.title: tree-sitter backend
items.description: The treeSitter() backend factory (highlight-engine-matrix, 2026-09-06): incremental-parsing grammar trees + highlight queries — the premium-accuracy engine. MARKUP output (query captures → escaped spans with inline var(--tok-token-*); survives the print freeze). WASM rides the npm-asset channel: web-tree-sitter core + tree-sitter-{typescript,javascript} grammar binaries resolve through an explicit loader seam — wasmLoader(asset) > wasmBase prefix > the static four-entry ?url import map; the browser consumes bundler-emitted HTTP URLs, Node/vitest feeds real bytes (createRequire + readFile) — both initialize REAL wasm (ABI 14 grammar packages asserted in-window at runtime). Queries (.scm, upstream MIT, embedded byte-identical) compose PER GRAMMAR (javascript=JS+JSX, typescript=JS+TS, tsx=JS+TS+JSX — a JSX query against the plain TS grammar is a QueryError). Curated: typescript/tsx/javascript/jsx; langs allowlist per instance.

items.name: highlight-lang-detector
items.title: DLD default language detector (four-layer waterfall)
items.description: The default language detector (highlight-lang-detector, 2026-09-07): defaultLangDetector() runs a FOUR-LAYER waterfall — L1 filename (extension + exact-basename tables), L2 shebang / first-line modeline, L3 structural probes (Markdown-guarded; never a programming-language fingerprint), L4 betlang statistics (wasm) — where every layer is its OWN lazy module: a hit short-circuits and the deeper layers never load a byte. 'Four layers' counts the waterfall only; the card's DETECTION rings stay three (langDetector prop → HIGHLIGHT_DETECT_KEY context → backend.detector) plus the runtime-reject tail. betlangDetector() is L4 standalone (skip L1-L3 — plugins and explicit props compose it). lang-canonical.ts is the single authoritative table the layers and the betlang 48-label mapping all derive from. Detection is an OPTIONAL capability by the zero-build-edge law: a bare code-card consumer carries ZERO DLD bytes and lang='auto' rejects at runtime with install + wiring guidance; wire through the highlight-detect-default wrapper item (children form ①) or one hand-written setContext(HIGHLIGHT_DETECT_KEY, { detector: defaultLangDetector() }) (form ②). The wasm rides the @jixoai/ui-betlang-wasm npm package (betlang =0.1.1 pinned at the crate, checksum-gated build — supply chain = your lockfile).
items.docs: npx jixoai-ui add @jixoai/highlight-lang-detector — then import { defaultLangDetector } from '$lib/highlight/default-detector' (the waterfall; re-exports AUTO_LANG) or { betlangDetector } from '$lib/highlight/betlang-detector' (statistics only) and wire ONE line at any subtree root: setContext(HIGHLIGHT_DETECT_KEY, { detector: defaultLangDetector() }) — or install the highlight-detect-default wrapper item and wrap the subtree. The wasm channel: browsers load it through the package's own new-URL asset (vite dev AND build — never a hand-written ?url import, which breaks vite dev); Node/vitest read real bytes through createRequire (tests run real wasm, never a mock).

items.name: toc-outline
items.title: ToC outline derivation
items.description: The zero-handwritten-id half of automatic ToC linkage (scroll-area family, 2026-08-22): framework-free outline derivation from a content root's heading tree. Scans the configured levels (default h2/h3), slugifies labels with dedupe, stamps derived ids back onto the headings (fragment links need a real id), skips [data-toc-skip] subtrees, and exposes each entry's EXTENT (heading → next same-or-higher heading) for toc-engine's extents provider. tocOutlineToSections() collapses entries into toc.svelte's sections shape. items.name: scroll-area
items.title: Scroll area

Instance exports (bind:this): getViewport() / scrollTo().

(CSS length — inline ring padding, compensated against the reserved gutter), class/style + restProps passthrough to the viewport, children snippet. getViewport() feeds Toc scrollRoot / toc-outline root / toc-engine extents — the zero-boilerplate ToC pairing.
