items.name: scroll-run
items.title: Scroll run
items.description: The ONE scrollable-region system (Owner 2026-09-04, the unification — tabs and button-group are the first two consumers; every future scrollable strip reuses this, never a local copy). Three parts: scroll-run.svelte.ts (createScrollStamp, the JS half — the scrollability VERDICT stamped as data-jx-scroll-state none|start-closed|end-closed|open, the single truth the css gates every overlay on; per-member --jx-edge-start/end clipped-fraction factors + host --jx-scroll-progress, RTL-normalized; ResizeObserver + visibilitychange/focus wake for background tabs; the RTL three-engine canonical [−max,0] funnel detectRtlScrollModel/rtlScrollToCanonical/rtlScrollFromCanonical (inline axis only); nudgeRun, the padding-lane-aware page step on EITHER axis; the ScrollEffect builders ramp/progressBlur/shadow, the press-button effect convention); scroll-run.css (the law sheet — the run IS the scroller: data-jx-scroll-run + data-axis degrade any strip to a hidden-scrollbar scroll run inside its host's ONE-CELL GRID; the edge factors consumed SQUARED, the eased curve — ONE member-ramp builder ramp({ opacity, blur, translate }) with every toggle default ON and a turned-off toggle never paying its css property; the frosted edge chips and the merged veil layer with its scroll-driven translate entrance; the shadow veil on the separator INK law — backdrop contrast subtracts color, never adds black; pre-hydration hides every overlay, reduced-motion kills the translate only); scroll-chrome.svelte (ScrollChrome, the DOM half of the chrome — the veil layer (progressBlur ladder or shadow bands) + the two chevron chips as real focusable buttons, wired to nudgeRun). AXIS-AWARE (round 2): the run's data-axis picks the measuring axis — a VERTICAL run measures along the block axis (scrollTop, block lane, no RTL funnel), places its chips against the block edges — horizontally CENTERED, painting the up/down glyph slots and slides its veil entrance along the block axis; the progressBlur ladder rides EITHER axis (inline edges on a horizontal run, block-edge top/bottom bands on a vertical one — the component's grid dialect). Content that cannot scroll paints NOTHING: the none verdict gates every chip, and a childList MutationObserver re-verdicts when members come or go (a shrunk strip retires its chrome). The chips are CUSTOMIZABLE two ways: css-var glyph swaps (FOUR physical direction slots --jx-scroll-chevron-left/-right/-up/-down, each independently swappable; the run axis + the chip edge + page direction pick the slot, RTL swapping the inline pair) or backwardContent/forwardContent snippet children rendered INSIDE the frosted buttons (the frost, gating and focusable-button law stay; the glyph layer retires and the content centers in the chip). The chips sit IN-BOARD by default — flush against the edge they serve, centered on the cross axis, every placement rule zero-specificity so a consumer override re-places them; hover RAISES a chip (Owner round 10): the frost paints --jx-scroll-chevron-chip-hover (near-opaque) and the lift deepens (the transition carries only the hover pair — the scroll-driven fade never animates). The ramp magnitudes are CHROME-OWNED: ScrollChrome stamps --jx-scroll-edge-slide/blur on the run from the builder's distance/radius (a toggle off never sets its var — consumers never hand-write them). Either chip can be DECLARED disabled (backwardDisabled/forwardDisabled, default rendered): a disabled chip does not render AT ALL — no DOM node, no paint, no a11y entry (consumer-declared absence; the verdict stays the automatic gate for rendered chips). Consumers keep ONLY their tuning: their own band widths, snap, mirrors onto companion elements (tabs mirrors the factors onto its indicator so the bar rides its active trigger).
items.docs: Host contract: a ONE-CELL grid host (.jx-scroll-host, grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr)) stacking the run, the veil layer and the chips in one cell — grid positions, z-index layers, never position:*. The run (your strip's element) carries data-jx-scroll-run + data-axis and is the scroller itself. createScrollStamp(options): run, host, members() (the ramp audience), ramps (bool — stamp the per-member factors only for slide/blur/blurSlide), mirrors? (() => {target, source}[] — stamp a companion element with a member's factors, e.g. tabs' indicator), progressVar?. Builders: ramp({opacity=true, blur=true, translate=true, distance='8px', radius='4px'}) the ONE member-ramp (a toggle off never pays its property), progressBlur({blurLevels, width}) capped-ladder veil (inline axis), shadow({width}) the contrast-ink veil (both axes). ScrollChrome props: scrollEffect (a builder's product — this component OWNS the run's data-scroll-effect + data-ramp-* attrs), run (its data-axis drives axis awareness), backwardLabel/forwardLabel (REQUIRED accessible names), backwardContent/forwardContent (custom chip content snippets — frost/gating/button law stay). CSS knobs on the HOST (overlays are the run's siblings): --jx-scroll-veil (band width, default inset·1.5), --jx-scroll-edge-slide/--jx-scroll-edge-blur, --jx-scroll-chevron-* (chip ink/size/glyphs).

items.name: icon
items.title: Icon
items.description: The named-glyph renderer over the generated icon-set: <Icon name="chevronRight" /> paints 16px currentColor artwork with a typo-proof IconName union (a wrong name is a compile error). The component owns the <svg> root (viewBox from the data, square size edge, caps/joins by artwork nature, aria-hidden, data-jx-icon); class + rest props land on the root verbatim; size and strokeWidth are props, never wrapper CSS. Inline-core names render synchronously (SSR paints them, hydration matches, zero wiring); names past the chunk budget ride loadIcon() into a FIXED reserved box — pending and rejected render the identical span so hydration never rewrites it, and a failed chunk warns once per session.
items.docs: Props: name (required IconName from '$lib/icon-set.gen' — typos are compile errors), size? (number | string, resolved through IconDefaults' open literal slot — explicit ?? own 16; numeric sizes px-coerce on the lazy pending box), strokeWidth? (default 2, stroke artwork only), class? + rest spread onto the <svg> root. Decorative by contract (aria-hidden baked in; meaning lives in surrounding text or the control's aria-label). Lazy failures warn once per chunk per session and keep the reserved box — never a layout shift.

items.name: icon-button
items.title: Icon button
items.description: The icon+text button with an explicit two-part contract: icon is the glyph (ALWAYS decorative — wrapped aria-hidden), text is the ONE label (a single string, single-sourced). Two postures: text (icon + label side by side) and iconOnly (a square on the same 42px band as a text button — the label moves to the tooltip and stays the accessible name via aria-label; an icon-only button must say itself). Composed ON press-button: every paint variant and effect loop, href/external anchoring and the press law pass through verbatim.
items.docs: Props: icon (required snippet — the glyph, always decorative), text (required string — the one label), variant? (press-button paint union, default 'outline'), iconOnly? (boolean — square posture: text moves to the tooltip AND stays aria-label), placement? (tooltip side, icon-only only), arrow? (the tip's aimed pointer notch — ON by default, opt out for plain bubbles), effect? (shimmer/pulse/rainbow/ripple — inherited), href?, external?, onclick?, type?, class?. Composed ON press-button: every capability passes through verbatim; the icon-only square rides the same 42px band (size-10.5).

items.name: progressive-blur
items.title: Progressive blur
items.description: The scroll-edge blur atom (Magic UI port, 2026-08-25): stacked masked backdrop-filter bands ramp blur from clear at the inner edge to the full stack at the scrollport edge — content scrolling under its OWN container's edge diffuses instead of slicing. The overlay root is a sticky h-0 pin (zero layout impact, glued to the scrollport edge; abspos-in-scroller scrolls away), so the whole component is markup + css, zero JS. jixoai extension: reveal='scroll' fades the ladder in with the CSS scroll timeline (nothing blurs at rest) — @supports-gated, degrading to no effect. pin='grid' (2026-09-01): a position-free dialect for one-cell grid hosts (start/end/inline positions, gradients aim physically, documented LTR) with a hold option (the outer share of the band, %, that keeps the ladder's peak instead of ramping — for strips whose readable content parks inboard of a control lane). Grid-dialect paint law (empirical, Chromium 152): the band painted after the scroller and a no-op translateZ(0) compositor isolation per band — without these a veil at the scroll-origin edge samples a dead backdrop and only the first band after the scroller paints; the ladder layers themselves stay pure grid items of the band.
items.docs: Drop as an EARLY CHILD of the scroll container. Props: position? ('bottom' default | 'top' | 'both' | 'start' | 'end' | 'inline' — the latter three hang from the inline edges; inline bands pair best with pin='grid'), pin? ('sticky' default, the zero-layout root inside a scroller | 'grid' — the position-free dialect: the band is a grid-area 1/1 sibling in the consumer's one-cell host, start/end only), height? (any definite CSS length, default 6rem — % unsupported: the band resolves against the 0-height sticky root), blurLevels? (px ladder inner-edge first, default [0.5,1,2,4,8,16,32,64], ≥2), reveal? ('static' default = always painted | 'scroll' = scroll-timeline fade over --jx-pblur-ramp, 72px default), class?.

items.title: Button group
items.description: Joined action layout container: orientation/justify shell that presses edge-to-edge press-buttons (and icon-buttons) over the hairline seam law — adjacent children collapse borders via a -1px margin so a joined row of outline buttons reads as ONE control with 1px seams, never a 2px double border. The container owns NOTHING but layout and seam: buttons keep their own paint (variant ladder, press physics, density tier); the group paints no bezel. role=group with a required label (grouping of related actions, never a selection surface — joined selection is toggle-group). A joined row is fundamentally a CONTAINER, so it owns the overflow question (Owner 2026-09-04): overflow='wrap' (default, multi-row flow with the seam law per row), overflow='collapse' (measured collapse into a dropdown tail — buttons that no longer fit re-home into an overflow menu, dividers fence the tail), or overflow='scroll' (a hidden-scrollbar scroll run on the shared @jixoai/scroll-run system — data-jx-scroll-run IS the group root, the JS-stamped verdict gates the frosted edge chips, and scrollEffect picks the edge treatment via the same builder convention as tabs: ramp() the ONE member-ramp builder ({ opacity, blur, translate } toggles, all default on), progressBlur()/shadow() the veil pair — and the chrome is AXIS-AWARE: a vertical scroll group rides the same contract against its block edges).
items.docs: Props: label (REQUIRED aria name), orientation ('horizontal'|'vertical'), justify ('start'|'end'|'center'|'between'), density, class. ROLE LAW: root is role=group — actions keep their own tab stops and activation; the group adds NO selection semantics (joined selection is toggle-group's contract). Composition: children are plain PressButton/icon-button instances; ButtonGroupDivider inserts a 1px seam member. Paint: the shared seam lives in button-group.css keyed on the data-jx-bgroup hook (Tier-2 vocabulary consumed-only).

items.name: input-group
items.title: Input group
items.description: The joined field shell — ONE 1px var(--border) bezel, the var(--background) fill, hover lift, inset focus ring and invalid dashed border ride the SAME paint as the shared html-control-shell law (state machines in input-group.css keyed on the data-jx-igroup hook). A composition frame, not a closed composite: InputGroupAddon lanes (hairline seams per addon edge — no double borders by construction), InputGroupInput as the native input member, press-buttons ride the inline-end addon. disabled on the ROOT disables the whole group natively (InputGroupInput renders disabled, every addon renders inert — the platform's containment).
items.docs: Props (root): label (REQUIRED a11y name), name/value/bind:value forwarded to the InputGroupInput member, disabled (native propagation: input renders disabled, addons render inert), invalid, density, class. Members: InputGroupAddon (align 'inline-start'|'inline-end', decorative lane), InputGroupInput (the native input — its own name= submits through the input family contract, MULTIVALUE-ready via the form-field seam when composed so). The shell is a composition frame: children compose freely inside the lane; seams are the addons' hairlines, the shell carries exactly one border.

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.description: Terminal-native charts, zero runtime dependencies: horizontal block-glyph bars on the mono text grid (label + value lanes, fill/tonal/outline ink), one-line sparklines (block or braille cells), an SVG polyline over hairline grid rules (optional 12% tonal area, non-scaling round markers, axes as authored snippet slots — never guessed), and a stroke-dasharray donut ring in the --chart-1..5 semantic palette with a neutral brand-hue oklch ladder. Deterministic display primitives: every degenerate input (empty, all-negative, constant, NaN, zero-total) has a frozen, unit-tested output; each part is role=img with a REQUIRED label and an opt-in visually-hidden data table fallback. The glyph math exports from the folder for tests; the Chart root only shares a density tier.
items.docs: Props (all parts): data (readonly number[], required), label (string, REQUIRED accessible name — no default by contract), table? (opt-in visually-hidden data table fallback), density?, class?, ...rest. ChartBar: labels? (parallel label lane), variant? ('fill'|'tonal'|'outline' through the global hue slots), cells? (bar budget in character cells, default 20), values? (value lane, default true). ChartSparkline: cells? ('block'|'braille', default 'braille'). ChartLine: area?, markers? (default true), xAxis?/yAxis? (authored axis snippets). ChartDonut: size? (96), thickness? (12), children? (center slot). Chart root: density? (provided to the subtree). Pure math exported from the folder for tests.

items.name: pattern-login
items.title: Pattern login
items.description: The `ssh user@host` login card — a composition product, not a primitive: user/host lanes are plain Input (innerInlineStart carries the user@ / --host= glyphs), the passphrase reveal rides the Input's own eye (hard F1 prerequisite — no pattern-local fallback), the OTP second-factor screen rides input-otp (joined form value; incomplete codes submit empty), the submit is a PressButton, and the footer is the copyable npx bootstrap line — the terminal idiom's magic-link analog.
items.docs: Barrel: default = the login card; PatternLoginOtp = the 2FA screen. Card props: host/user/password (bindable), command, onsignin?, children? (extra lanes). OTP props: host, length (6), value (bindable), hint?, onverify?(code).

items.name: pattern-pricing
items.title: Pattern pricing
items.description: The `$ plan --compare` section: the comparison matrix rides the Table family (consumer authors thead/tbody; the recommended column opts in with data-jx-recommended on the th AND its td's — pattern css paints brand inset rules that keep the row-hover law intact), each tier's install command rides a CodeCard with a copy PressButton in its footer, plan labels ride Badge. Commands/labels are value-domain payload; no atom is patched.
items.docs: Props: tiers (readonly PricingTier[]: plan, command, recommended?, note?), children (the thead/tbody snippet — the Table contract), eyebrow?, caption?, class?. The heading stays out of the pattern; the page owns its h2.

items.name: pattern-hero-set
items.title: Pattern hero set
items.description: Three hero forms of the terminal grammar: the terminal-window hero (hero-section with the right column prewired to a terminal-card whose command derives from copyCommand — one string drives the CTA label, the clipboard payload and the typed demo), the ASCII-art headline hero (art as whitespace-preserved payload in a pre under the mono scale law — wide banners scroll, ascii never reflows), and the badge-marquee hero (plain mono token strip with an aria-hidden duplicate on a seamless -50% CSS loop; prefers-reduced-motion kills the animation, folds the duplicate away and leaves a static scrollable row).
items.docs: Barrel: default = the terminal-window hero (eyebrow, summary, copyCommand required; title/badges/secondary snippets forwarded; barTitle/outputs/theme/speed for the terminal). PatternHeroAscii: art required, cta/secondary label+href. PatternHeroMarquee: items required, title? snippet, duration (24s).

items.name: pattern-faq
items.title: Pattern faq
items.description: The man-page FAQ: a command(section) head with the print-style dotted NAME leader over the accordion family (native details/summary — exclusive by default, questions compose as AccordionItem children or bare details), closing on a SEE ALSO line. The pattern owns only the framing; disclosure semantics, keyboard and SSR state belong to the accordion.
items.docs: Props: children (the questions — AccordionItem parts), command? ('jixoai-ui-faq'), section? ('7'), summary?, exclusive? (true), seeAlso? (snippet — compose links), class?.

items.name: pattern-cta
items.title: Pattern cta
items.description: The shell-prompt CTA band: a lead block (eyebrow / heading / summary / optional outline escape) beside the install command on a CodeCard (copyable=false — the band owns exactly ONE copy affordance) with the copy PressButton in the card's footer: fill rung, copy → check flip, 1.4s copied surface. Press physics stay the button's own.
items.docs: Props: command ('npx jixoai-ui init'), heading?, summary?, actionLabel? ('copy command'), secondaryLabel?/secondaryHref? (renders the outline escape when set), class?.

items.name: entity
items.title: Entity context
items.description: The entity law as a Context channel: border is objecthood — depth accumulates through provideEntity() (dialog panels, popovers), form shells dissolve at depth 1, hairlines auto-reassert at depth 2+, and [data-assert-border] force-spends the budget. Background rides the same restraint: transparency first, backdrop-filter as the tint.

items.name: katex
items.title: KaTeX math engine (isomorphic)
items.description: Thin KaTeX integration — explicitly NOT a wrapper (the lib/shiki precedent): renderTex forwards katex.renderToString with the engine's option vocabulary untouched under jixoai defaults that every caller can override key-for-key (output 'htmlAndMathml', throwOnError:false — invalid TeX paints in place, errorColor 'var(--error)' — the token binding), registerMacros extends the TeX vocabulary site-wide (a module-level table, last-wins per key), and the ONE side effect makes math out-of-the-box: import 'katex/dist/katex.min.css' — KaTeX's fonts ride the npm package and the consumer's bundler, so both math surfaces (and any future markdown lane) load engine css + fonts exactly once via $lib/katex. Synchronous and isomorphic: the math surfaces bake REAL markup during SSR/prerender — no plain-text floor, no hydration work (the load-bearing lane ruling this lib carries).
items.docs: Based on KaTeX (npm: katex) — this lib adds loading + default strategy only, never re-interprets KaTeX output; a site that wants output:'mathml' or throwOnError:true gets exactly that. jixoai defaults (each overridable by the same-key option): output 'htmlAndMathml' (visual HTML plus the hidden MathML — the screen-reader path, so surfaces mount no aria-label), throwOnError:false (the bad source run paints in the errorColor), errorColor 'var(--error)'. registerMacros({ '\\RR': '\\mathbb{R}' }) at app boot merges the site-level macro table (last-wins per key; a per-call macros option layers on top). The css + font side effect lives HERE, not in each ui item: `import { renderTex } from '$lib/katex'` is the one import a math-bearing site needs.

items.name: mermaid-engine
items.title: Mermaid diagram engine (lazy)
items.description: Lazy Mermaid integration — explicitly NOT a wrapper: ONE dynamic import('mermaid') singleton (the ~1MB DOM-bound engine code-splits and loads only when a diagram actually renders; a failed load clears the memo and retries), token-derived theming through the probe + parseColor pipeline (hidden probes INSIDE the passed root resolve live var() chains via getComputedStyle; @jixoai/color-utils converts to mermaid-safe hex; an unparseable token degrades to its committed per-theme safe-hex fallback — never a raw string, so theming never breaks a render), a ONE-SOURCE-PER-FIELD themeVariables table on theme 'base', and engine discipline: initialize/render pairs serialize through ONE rejection-recovering promise chain (a failed render never poisons the next), a fingerprint over the FINAL merged initialize payload skips redundant initialize (a brand-hue or token change inside the SAME theme mode still re-runs it — stale colors are impossible), the protected fields (startOnLoad:false · securityLevel:'strict' · theme:'base') survive any consumer config, and render ids follow the collision contract (per-instance monotonic base + per-render suffix — two instances, same names, and consecutive re-renders never share a live id). An explicit resolvedTheme reads the TARGET sheet through a temporary local probe wrapper — never a global class mutation.
items.docs: renderDiagram(source, { id, theme, config, themeRoot }) — BROWSER-ONLY (an SSR call rejects with an explicit browser-only diagnostic inside MermaidRenderError.diagnostic; every failure normalizes there). The surface passes its OWN container as themeRoot so scoped containers resolve their tokens, never the page's. The consumer's config is mermaid's own MermaidConfig and merges below the protected fields and the derived palette (user themeVariables overlay FIELD-WISE over the derived defaults). `import { renderDiagram, readThemeTokens } from '$lib/mermaid-engine'`; ids come from createRenderIdMinter(name).next() — the collision contract.

items.name: math-inline
items.title: Math inline
items.description: The inline math surface: ONE native <span> carrying real KaTeX markup rendered SYNCHRONOUSLY — the isomorphic-small SSR lane (prerender bakes the formula itself: no plain-text floor, no hydration work, no flash; a tex prop change re-derives live). No chrome, no controls; the span inherits prose currentColor — light/dark inverts with ZERO re-render. role="math" sits on the content-only span with katex's hidden MathML as the screen-reader path (no aria-label shadowing); consumer attributes spread through first — data-testid/title/aria-*/handlers land untouched while the component's semantic stamps win their own fields.
items.docs: Props: tex (required), macros?, strict?, trust?; rest flows to the native <span>. The engine css + fonts ride the $lib/katex import (the lib item arrives with the install — one side effect, both math surfaces). Invalid TeX paints in place through the facade's throwOnError:false default; a caller-forced throw degrades to the escaped raw source + one console.warn.

items.name: math-block
items.title: Math block
items.description: The display math surface: a native <figure> (figure semantics kept) framing a wide-equation strip that rides the SHARED scroll-run contract wholesale — createScrollStamp's verdict (data-jx-scroll-state none|start-closed|end-closed|open) gates ScrollChrome's shadow veil and nudge chips, so a formula that fits paints no chrome — with real KaTeX markup rendered SYNCHRONOUSLY during SSR/prerender (the isomorphic-small lane: true zero flash, zero CLS, print-freeze-safe markup — NOT code-card's floor-then-upgrade), a copy control carrying the raw TeX source (press physics, clipboard fallback, labels localization payload), and errors painted IN PLACE (the errorColor token run inside the same box, one console.warn diagnostic; a caller-forced throw degrades to the raw source — errors never escape a component boundary).
items.docs: Props: tex (required), copyable=true, labels? ({copy?, copied?}), macros?, strict?, trust?; rest flows to the figure. The strip rides the scroll-run law verbatim: the run is the scroller (data-jx-scroll-run + data-axis="horizontal" inside a one-cell grid host), the stamp machine arms on hydration and re-verdicts when a wider formula lands. role="math" lives on the inner content-only wrapper — the copy button stays a discoverable node. Engine css + fonts ride the $lib/katex import.

items.name: mermaid
items.title: Mermaid diagram
items.description: The diagram surface under the code-card progressive-enhancement law: prerender paints the escaped diagram source as a readable zero-JS floor, hydration lazy-loads the engine (the mermaid-engine singleton, ~1MB code-split) and swaps in the sanitized SVG with a reduced-motion-respecting fade over a min-height reserve (--jx-mermaid-floor-min, consumer-tunable). Theme follows the flip AUTOMATICALLY: the surface passes its own figure as the engine's themeRoot (scoped containers resolve THEIR tokens) and an effective-scope observer re-renders on any ancestor theme change — explicit 'light'/'dark' pins read the target sheet through a local wrapper. Zoom (±0.25 steps, clamp 0.5–3, reset) is a pure transform with the viewport as the two-axis pan surface — the recorded scroll-run exemption (thin token scrollbars both axes, NO shared chrome inside), plus a copy-source control with the labels localization payload. A parse failure paints the error summary strip and KEEPS the source floor standing.
items.docs: Props: source (required — a runtime prop, the code-card rule), name? (head tab label + render-id base), theme='auto' ('light'|'dark' pin), copyable=true, zoomable=true, labels? ({copy, copied, zoomIn, zoomOut, zoomReset, renderError, diagram — the viewport's accessible name when name is absent}), config? (mermaid's own MermaidConfig — the engine's precedence ladder applies); rest flows to the figure. data-state rides floor|rendering|rendered|error; the viewport keeps role="img" with a NON-EMPTY accessible name at all times (the trimmed ladder name → labels.diagram → 'Diagram').
